newsitem.title: FRANCE: FEATURE - Jaguar XK8 faces uphill sales struggle.
newsitem.headline: FEATURE - Jaguar XK8 faces uphill sales struggle.

text.p: A flame red Ferrari driven by a stunning movie star.
A silver Porsche storming down the autobahn at 250 kph (155 mph).
Anyone with an interest in cars will probably have an immediate picture in their minds when these charismatic and successful cars are mentioned.
Try Maserati. "That's a famous old Italian sports car. Are they still around?." Just barely, selling less than 2,000 cars a year.
Lotus. "Didn't it win a few Grand Prix once?"
Jaguar. In Britain, that could conjure up visions of rusting, unreliable and incompetently built cars from the 70s and 80s.

But Jaguar is about to fill its showrooms around the world with its new $65,000 plus XK8 coupes and convertibles. It hopes that any word assocation at this week's Paris car show, where it launches XK8 sales, will centre on its glamorous old marques like the legendary "E" type, or the XK120.
If not, Jaguar will have a hard time making money with the new car, according to industry analysts.
"Image is all in the luxury sports car market," says Peter Schmidt, analyst with Automotive Industry Data in Britain.
Being owned by a mass car maker like Ford can't help. Jaguar was taken over by the the second biggest car maker in America for $2.5 billion in 1989.
Schmidt says that the sector is dying and only ultra desirable products can be successful.

"Sports cars are a dying and shrinking market. If you plot the sales of say the Toyota Supra, sales are falling like a stone. And people's tastes are changing in Europe and America. They don't want to flaunt their wealth; the wives of the rich are even wearing their fur coats inside out," Schmidt said.

Jaguar chairman Nick Scheele has said he hopes to sell 12,000 XK8s a year, mainly in the U.S. The price has yet to be announced, but the 4.0 litre V8's predessor the XJ-S sold for between $65,000 and $75,000.

Competition will be formidable. Apart from Ferraris and Porsches at the high-priced end of the market, there will be attacks from below with entrants like Mercedes with its little SLK, and the BMW MZ3, a souped up version of its U.S.-made two seater.
Some analysts see some positive signs for the XK8, particularly in the U.S.

"The U.S. looks pretty positive for the launch of the XK8. The market there is buoyant, Porsche is selling reasonably strongly there at the moment," said Ian Robertson of London's Economist Intelligence Unit.
"The current competition in the U.S., the Mercedes SL, Porsche 911, Honda NSX, BMW 8 are looking a bit tired, so some new blood should lead to incremental sales," said Robertson.
But Robertson also sees a shadow over the future for these high performance cars.

"Environmental measures like a long-mooted carbon fuel tax in Europe could spell the end of these big, high performance vehicles. And there's another negative. The sector immediately below -- the Porsche Boxster (also introduced at the Paris show) and smaller Mercedes, some buyers might opt for these more environmentally friendly types," says Robertson.
Tougher rules on the environment might force Jaguar, and other sports car makers, to seek new buyers in booming new economies like the Far East.
"Outside of Europe there are fewer concerns about fuel consumption, particularly in the U.S.," said John Lawson, European automotive analyst for Salomon Brothers.

"Vehicles that parade wealth and status are more fashionable in emerging markets. The sports and luxury car makers should concentrate more on opening up and servicing them where environmental concerns are not so pressing," said Lawson.
But Schmidt believes Jaguar will have a hard time meeting its targets.

"After an initial flurry of registrations, many I'm sure among senior Ford executives, I don't feel confident that Jaguar will succeed -- 12,000 is a tall order and in my view it will be exceedingly difficult for them to achieve these sales," he said.
Jaguar will have an initial boost to its sales in the U.S.
Luxury store chain Neiman Marcus has included a special edition of the XK8 on its Christmas catalogue.
It is offering 50 Titanium painted XK8s with extras including a Harman Kardon sound system, chrome wheels, lambswool footwell rugs and a convertible wind deflector. Each costs $74,975 before taxes.
